interfaces.singleton: Every mark except rho0 fixes a. The complete critical singleton reduction, with explicit smaller-degree induction, supplies n=2r>=14 and the actual natural alternating omission in the contrary range.
interfaces.prefix_growth: Far commutation and fixation of a fix the entire prefix orbit. Failure of strict growth would make that orbit ambient invariant; its being the whole set would contradict an intransitive maximal omission. No alternating prefix kernel is assumed.
interfaces.later_cut: The actual suffix fixes the prefix orbit of a. A single ambient edge gives exactly two omission orbits and all shared labels lie below the cut.
interfaces.reversal: The actual reversed preceding subgroup fixes the old prefix orbit, so the complete transitive-side or intransitive-side support theorem applies at an interior cut. The endpoint support theorem is used separately at j=r-1. Both exclude g=0, and give support(P_(g-1))<=2g+1.
interfaces.small_prefix: An intransitive P1 on at most five moved points has literal 3+2 orbits. Evenness identifies both marks and far commutation preserves the exterior pair under the entire group, contradicting transitivity.
interfaces.dihedral: The remaining actual P1 is the natural D10. The critical-dihedral-tail lemma, inside the complete transitive-tail proof, is applied at the ORIGINAL cut in full reversal with h=r-3 and n-5=2h+1. No neighboring unique-cut or transitive-suffix hypothesis is inferred from a supported D10 head.

new_statements: Strict prefix growth from the singleton point and literal suffix fixation.
The two actual omission orbits and one-sided shared labels at every later unique cut.
First shared indices zero, one and two are impossible in the contrary rank range.
contributions: The source cut strategy, complete support inequalities and critical-dihedral proof remain acquired. The point-based prefix argument and literal exterior-pair obstruction are this continuation. No independent claim of a pure alternating kernel is made.
